newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban make nine new government appointments.
newsitem.headline: Taleban make nine new government appointments.

text.p: The leader of Afghanistan's Taleban, Mullah Mohammad Omar, has made nine new appointments to his administration.

Mullah Omar appointed on Tuesday four new acting ministers, two deputy ministers, two provincial governors and a divisional commander, acting information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told a news conference on Tuesday.

The ministerial appointments were made in an acting capacity. Mullah Omar says the Taleban administration is an interim government pending a meeting of all Afghan leaders to decide how to form a broad-based national government.

Two of the appointments replace earlier incumbents: Qari Din Mohammed replaces Mawlavi Hafizullah at the Ministry of Planning and Mawlavi Abdul Raqib replaces Mullah Abdul Sattar at the Ministry of Refugee Repatriation.

Mutaqi did not give any explanation for the changes. The Taleban control three-quarters of Afghanistan and are still fighting a northern alliance of Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum and former goverment military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
The appointments are as follows:
ACTING MINISTERS
Qari Din Mohammed.........acting Minister of Planning
Mawlavi Abdul Raqib.......acting Minister for Refugee
Repatriation
Mawlavi Abdul Bakh........acting Minister of Martyrs and
Disabled
Mawlavi Mohammed Rustam...acting Minister of Urban
Reconstruction
ACTING DEPUTY MINISTERS
Mawlavi Isatullah.........acting Deputy Minster of Planning
Mawlavi Abdul Salaam......acting Deputy Minster of Labour
and Social Affairs
GOVERNORS
Mawlavi Karamatullah......Governor of Paktia province
Mawlavi Shamshuddin.......Governor of Paktika
MILITARY
Mawlavi Mohammed Zahir....Commander of 4th Armoured Division
(Note - Mawlavi is the title given to a senior mullah, or Islamic priest).
